Introspection

/in-truh-SPEK-shun/ — stress on SPEK · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Introspection is the act of closely examining one's own thoughts and feelings.

After losing the debate, Maya spent the weekend in quiet introspection.

Worked Example

After flunking the chemistry exam, Jordan spent hours in introspection, analyzing what he'd done wrong.

Intro- (inward) + spect (look) + -ion (act of) = the act of looking inward. We direct our gaze inside ourselves at our thoughts and feelings. The same spect root appears in inspect (look into), spectator (one who looks), and spectacles (tools for looking). Intro- also shows up in introduce (bring inward) and introvert (turned inward).

How Introspection Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

self-reflection

self-reflection: calmly thinking over your own actions

soul-searching

soul-searching: deep, often painful questioning of your conscience

contemplation

contemplation: long, quiet, focused thinking about something

Antonyms

impulsiveness

impulsiveness: acting without examining your own thoughts first

How Strong Is It? — daydreaming → pondering → reflection → introspection

daydreaming vs. introspection

daydreaming vs. introspection: Daydreaming lets your mind drift anywhere it likes, but introspection deliberately turns your attention onto your own thoughts and feelings.

pondering vs. introspection

pondering vs. introspection: You might spend an afternoon pondering a tricky math puzzle, while introspection means examining what is happening inside yourself.

reflection vs. introspection

reflection vs. introspection: A quick reflection on your day skims the surface; true introspection digs into why you felt and acted the way you did.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — intro-

Prefix — intro-: inward; within (Latin)

Root — spect

Root — spect: to look — from Latin specere/spectare, 'to look at' (Latin)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: the act or process of — turns a verb into a noun (Latin (-io, -ionem))

Put it together

Put it together: This is one of this unit's two special triple-decomposition words — three reusable parts instead of the usual two: intro- (inward) + spect (look) + -ion (the act or process of) = the act of looking inward at your own thoughts and feelings. The same spect root shows up whenever English talks about looking.

Use the root in a new word: inspector

Use the root in a new word: inspector: The building inspector looked over every beam and wire before declaring the new gym safe.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal/neutral

Use introspection when someone is examining their own thoughts and feelings—after a conflict, before a big decision, or in therapy. It emphasizes careful, inward self-examination, not daydreaming or casual self-thinking.
